statement: Yoga arises only for one whose mind is unclouded: turbidity of mind (kaluṣa) keeps yoga from arising as he practises.
subject: obs:kalusa

statement: Once yoga has arisen, the powers arise for him: seeing, hearing, thinking and knowing at a distance, omniscience, swiftness of mind, taking forms at will and acting without organs.
subject: cpt:pasupata-yoga
condition: for one constantly yoked; in abundance after six months (5.12-13)
notes: 1.21-26 opens with 'then', following the arising of yoga in 1.18-20; 5.12-13 adds that for one constantly yoked for six months it arises in abundance.

statement: Through conquest of the senses (indriya-jaya) he comes to be unattached, a yogin, constant in self, unborn and friendly.
subject: trm:indriya-jaya

statement: For one who is self-controlled, yoga proceeds from reciting the chosen verse, the Raudrī or the Bahurūpī Gāyatrī.
subject: prc:raudri-gayatri-japa
notes: The same sūtra group adds meditation on Oṃ with the fixation (dhāraṇā) held in the heart; see the result.

statement: Being insulted (paribhava) makes the wise one complete in austerity (kṛtsna-tapas).
subject: trm:paribhava

statement: The Pāśupata Sūtra holds that the ascetic is freed from sin through others' reviling of him: he gives his sin (pāpa) to them and takes their merit (puṇya).
subject: prc:courting-dishonour
notes: 4.13-15: for him this censure is no censure, so he should wander censured, his deeds uncensured.

statement: Dishonour (asanmāna) is declared the highest of all restraints.
subject: trm:asanmana

statement: Having cut with the intellect the root of the net of causes of the faults and fixed the whole mind on Rudra, alone, secure, free from sorrow and vigilant, he reaches the end of sufferings (duḥkhānta) through the Lord's grace (prasāda).
subject: trm:prasada
condition: when the root of the causes of the faults has been cut with the intellect and the whole mind is fixed on Rudra, with vigilance

corresponds.note: Kauṇḍinya adds that knowledge, dispassion, merit, lordship or renunciation alone do not suffice.

statement: Joyful and not heedless (apramatta), he attains greatness in each and every observance.
subject: trm:apramada

statement: Having gone by this rule (vidhi) to the proximity of Rudra (rudra-samīpa), no brahmin returns again.
subject: cpt:pasupata-vidhi

statement: The perfected yogin is not stained by action or by sin.
subject: cpt:pasupata-yoga

statement: Dwelling in the cremation ground, righteous and living on whatever he obtains, he attains union (sāyujya) with Rudra.
subject: prc:smasana-vasa

statement: The observance is the supreme gift, the supreme sacrifice and the supreme austerity, and leads to the supreme goal; therefore one should practise austerity more, with devotion to Śaṅkara alone.
subject: cpt:pasupata-vidhi

statement: The whole teaching is summed up in five categories: the end of suffering, the effect (the bound souls), the cause (the Lord), union (yoga) and the rule (vidhi).
subject: cpt:pancartha-five-categories

statement: Kauṇḍinya: the end of suffering (duḥkhānta) is attained by the Lord's grace (prasāda), not merely by knowledge, dispassion, merit, lordship or renunciation.
subject: trm:prasada

corresponds.note: The sūtra 5.35-40 on which this rests.

statement: The bound souls' paśu-state (paśutva) is bondage, a beginningless lack of lordship (anaiśvarya).
subject: obs:pasutva

statement: Conscious beings other than the Lord are 'paśus' because they see only the body and are bound by the kalās called effects and instruments.
subject: cpt:pasupata-kalas

shows_as.text: Seeing only the body: the paśu is so called because it 'sees' (only the body).

notes: Kauṇḍinya counts even those liberated by Sāṃkhya-Yoga, and all from Brahmā down to the animals, as paśus.

statement: The Lord produces the effect all at once or in sequence as he wills, depending neither on karma nor on the person; those who seek the fruits of action depend on him.
subject: cpt:pasupata-karana

statement: Playing is the Lord's nature, as heat is fire's; in play he produces, favours and conceals the threefold effect: knowledge-quality, part and soul (vidyā, kalā, paśu).
subject: cpt:isvara-krida-pasupata

statement: The disciple approaches the teacher because he is overcome by sufferings and seeks their end, not dharma, wealth, pleasure or isolation (kaivalya); the teacher's teaching is for grace.
subject: obs:duhkha-traya

shows_as.text: Asking whether there is a final and absolute removal of all sufferings: bodily-mental, from beings and from the gods (Kuśika's question).

statement: The rule (vidhi) begins with ash, has censure in its middle and ends with [feigned] folly; its three limbs are gift, worship and austerity.
subject: cpt:pasupata-vidhi

statement: Kauṇḍinya sets the practice in five stages (in the temple, among people, in an empty house or cave, in the cremation ground, in Rudra), each with its own residence, livelihood, strength, action, purification and gain.
subject: cpt:pasupata-five-stages

statement: The five means (residence, meditation, restraint of all organs, remembrance, grace) remove the five impurities (ignorance, demerit, habituation to objects, non-attainment of steadiness, lack of lordship), each stage yielding its gain.
subject: cpt:pasupata-five-means
notes: The stage descriptions give each stage's purification and gain; the closing verses list the five means, impurities, gains and places in the same order.

statement: In the fourth stage, in the cremation ground, remembrance (of Rudra) is the action, removal of forgetfulness the purification, and union with Rudra the gain.
subject: prc:rudra-anusmarana

statement: Kauṇḍinya holds that in the second stage, among people, closing the doors of the senses and acting like a madman destroy sin, the gain being the whole of dharma.
subject: prc:indriya-dvara-pidhana
prc:unmatta-carana

statement: Only once he has gained knowledge, his impurity is reduced and he has the teacher's leave does the ascetic go among people to court dishonour.
subject: nd:pasupata:fitness-for-the-second-stage
notes: The same passage: when people despise him on this false charge, their merit comes to him and his sin goes to them; the feigned acts must not conflict with the restraints.

statement: Honour (māna) is of two kinds, pride of birth ('I am a brahmin') and pride in the esteem given to householders, and the teaching of the unmanifest sign forbids both; the single garment, going about like a wretch and the hidden vow exclude its grounds: wealth, kin, fame, deeds and learning.
subject: cpt:courting-dishonour

shows_as.text: Pride of birth ('I am a brahmin'), pride in the esteem given to householders, and pride resting on wealth, kin, fame, deeds and learning.

statement: What the practitioner shares with cows and deer is endurance of the pairs of opposites (dvandva): bodily, from beings and from the gods.
subject: trm:dvandvajaya

statement: Heedlessness (pramāda) is inattention to what is to come and dependence; vigilance (apramāda) is like guarding a sprout.
subject: trm:apramada

shows_as.text: Inattention to what is to come, and dependence.

statement: The sufferings to be ended are those of oneself, bodily (illnesses) and mental (anger, greed, delusion, fear, despondency, envy, hatred, pride and the like), those from beings and those from the gods; and, fivefold, womb, birth, ignorance, old age and death.
subject: trm:duhkha

shows_as.text: Mental suffering as anger, greed, delusion, fear, despondency, envy, hatred and pride; bodily suffering as illness.

statement: The powers such as distant sight arise gradually, one after another, as a needle-point pierces a stack of a hundred lotus petals in succession.
subject: cpt:pasupata-yoga

statement: Ordinary gifts of cows, land and gold have uncertain, non-final and graded fruits; the gift of oneself (ātmapradāna) is supreme because it brings the certain and final attainment of Rudra's proximity, whose fruit is non-return.
subject: prc:atmapradana

statement: Where other systems teach isolation (kaivalya), the Pāśupata end of suffering brings the powers of knowing and acting and a lordship beyond kaivalya; the causes other systems name (primal matter, the person, time, nature) are here effects.
subject: cpt:duhkhanta

statement: The restraints are non-harming, celibacy, truthfulness, non-dealing (asaṃvyavahāra) and non-stealing; the observances are non-anger, service of the teacher, purity, lightness of diet and vigilance; all ten count as restraints (yama).
subject: cpt:pasupata-yama-niyama
